summary: The bill amends the National Trails System Act to require the Interior Secretary to complete a feasibility study within one year, in consultation with the Bay Area Ridge Trail Council and relevant agencies, on designating the 550-mile Bay Area Ridge Trail as a national scenic trail.

scores.thoughts: The bill directs the Secretary of the Interior to complete a feasibility study within one year, which requires the federal government to expend resources on research, consultation, and reporting. This constitutes a minor expansion of government activity and associated spending, though the impact is limited to a single, time-bound study rather than ongoing programs.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.

The bill focuses on studying the designation of a scenic trail that traverses parks, open spaces, ridgelines, wetlands, forests, and other natural features, explicitly highlighting scenic, historic, and environmental qualities. This engages with environmental and conservation themes by promoting public access to protected natural areas, creating a modest alignment with expanded environmental protections and recreation policy.
